policy.density: N processes of one actor/program start together and are held at an equivalent post-execution point; each held process reads /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup once, then all are released and their output is checked. Scriptw: shared precompiled host, phase barrier after its second execution (one warmup) with the Store live. Node: the adapted source with a beforeExit preload. Porffor: its native executable at a ptrace exit stop.
policy.capacity: Summed PSS of N held processes is the resident memory they use together. marginal = (total(Nmax) - total(1)) / (Nmax - 1); fixed = total(1) - marginal; processes in M bytes = floor((M - fixed) / marginal). The 16 GiB figure gives all 16 GiB to these processes: no kernel, page-cache or OS reserve. USS (private clean + dirty) at Nmax is reported beside it.
policy.wall: Fresh sequential processes under GNU time, spawn to exit, actor order rotated per round; output checked. Scriptw runs the host, which hashes its own 200 MB executable for its identity report and executes the program four times (3 samples + 1 warmup, its minimum); both costs are reported separately. Scriptw run is the product CLI on a warm program cache: it reads the source and loads its cached native code instead of compiling it.
policy.steady: Per-entry wall in fresh Stores/contexts through the Porffor panel harnesses: 21 measured entries after 10 checked warmups, four processes per actor/program in two blocks (second reversed); median of process medians.
policy.source: Scriptw runs the original bytes with its print. Node and Porffor run the same print-to-console.log adapter the Porffor panel uses; the steady-state V8 harness provides print in its context instead.
policy.node_flags: Node default and lean (--v8-pool-size=0 --single-threaded-gc --max-semi-space-size=1): no V8 platform worker threads, single-threaded GC, 1 MiB semi-spaces. NODE_OPTIONS, compile cache and snapshots are unset; Scriptw runs its defaults.
